title: Which of two to ten divide this big number?
description: The number eight thousand five hundred and sixty sits on a card with the helpers two to ten beneath it. The last digits show which helpers divide it exactly, and Keeko's doubt, that only ten does, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the end of a number shows which small numbers divide it, with no long division. Watch for students who stop at ten and forget that five and two come with it.

source: Let us take 8560. Does it have any factors from 2 to 10 (2,
video_script.why: The child sees that the end digits of a number show its small factors, so no long division is needed.
video_script.substitution: Look at the last digits of the number and test each helper from two to ten against them.
video_script.anchor: a card with the number 8560 and the helpers 2 to 10 in a row beneath it
video_script.wrong_answer: only ten divides eight thousand five hundred and sixty
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says only ten divides the number because it ends in zero. Ten is two times five, so five and two divide it as well, and the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: Two, four, five, eight and ten divide eight thousand five hundred and sixty exactly

final_answer.spoken: two, four, five, eight and ten divide it exactly

maths_rules: 8560 ends in 0, so 10 divides it; 10 = 2 x 5, so 5 and 2 divide it too
3 x 2853 = 8559, one less than 8560, so 3 leaves 1 and 3 does not divide it; 6 needs 3, so 6 does not divide it
7 x 1222 = 8554, so 7 leaves 6; 9 x 951 = 8559, so 9 leaves 1
video_script.design: One idea: end digits show small factors. Assumes the child knows division and multiples. Wrong idea: only ten divides a number that ends in zero. The number card stays on the board to the end.

<bookmark mark='num'/>The number is eight thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of the numbers from two to ten divide it exactly, without long division?

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>A number that divides another number exactly is called a factor of it.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Four is a factor of twelve, because twelve divided by four is three.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which helpers are factors of the number.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, last digit 0: 10 divides 8560; 10 = 2 x 5, so 5 and 2 divide it too

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step one, look at the last digit. It is zero, so ten divides the number.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Ten is two times five, so five and two divide it as well.

marks.split: the number is cut into 8500 and 60
marks.hund: a hundred is shown as 25 groups of 4
marks.sixty: 60 is shown as 15 groups of 4 and the helper 4 is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, test four. Cut the number into eight thousand five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='hund'/>A hundred is twenty five fours, so every hundred splits into fours.
<bookmark mark='sixty'/>Sixty is fifteen fours, so four divides the number.

marks.split: the number is cut into 8000 and 560
marks.thou: a thousand is shown as 125 groups of 8
marks.five: 560 is shown as 70 groups of 8 and the helper 8 is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, test eight. Cut the number into eight thousand and five hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>A thousand is one hundred and twenty five eights.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five hundred and sixty is seventy eights, so eight divides the number.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, three, six, seven, nine: 3 x 2853 = 8559, one less than 8560; 7 x 1222 = 8554; 9 x 951 = 8559; none fits, and 6 needs 3

marks.three: 3 x 2853 = 8559 is written with a gap of one to 8560
marks.fail: the helpers 3 and 6 are crossed out
marks.nine: 9 x 951 = 8559 is written, short of 8560, and 7 and 9 are crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step four, try three, six, seven and nine.
Three times two thousand eight hundred and fifty three is eight thousand five hundred and fifty nine.
<bookmark mark='fail'/>That is one less than the number, so three fails.
Six needs three as well, so six fails too.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Seven times one thousand two hundred and twenty two is eight thousand five hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine times nine hundred and fifty one is eight thousand five hundred and fifty nine.
Neither one reaches the number.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two, four, five, eight and ten divide eight thousand five hundred and sixty exactly.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only ten divides eight thousand five hundred and sixty, because it ends in zero.
<bookmark mark='split'/>But ten is two times five, so five and two divide it too.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Whatever ten divides, five and two divide as well, and the end digits give more.
